newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares end mixed in lethargic trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares end mixed in lethargic trade.

text.p: ** (0100 GMT) - Indian stocks end mixed, trade dull
** Squaring up at National Stock Exchange on last day of
settlement pushes blue-chips higher
** Benchmark Bombay share index rises 19.61 pts or 0.63
percent to 3,118.95, off the day's low of 3,079.46
** HDFC, Ranbaxy and SKF Bearings report rise in profit for
the first half of 1996/97 (April-March)
** NSE index up 0.64 pct, Delhi index 0.98 pct, Madras
index falls 0.57 pct and Calcutta 0.54 pct
Indian stocks ended mixed in lacklustre trade on Tuesday as major playes kept away from the market, dealers said.
The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) closed 19.61 points or 0.63 percent higher at 3,118.95, off the day's low of 3,079.46.
Traders said market activity continued to be sluggish as dealers awaited the central bank's monetary policy due to be released at the week-end.
"Overall, there is no specific buying interest in the market," said a dealer at a Bombay-based brokerage firm.
Analysts expect the Reserve Bank of India to announce a one percent cut in the cash reserve ratios of banks, a move that may induce banks to cut their lending rates.
On Saturday, the central bank will announce the monetary policy for the second half of 1996/97 (April-March).
Meanwhile, HDFC, Ranbaxy Lab and SKF Bearings Ltd reported a rise in first half net profits for 1996/97 (April-March).
Shares of housing finance company HDFC gained 14.25 rupees to 2,175.25 rupees after the firm said its net profit rose 43 percent to 1.09 billion rupees.
Ranbaxy Lab shares were unchanged at 612.25 rupees after the pharmaceutical maker said its net profit was up 21 percent to 718 million rupees.
SKF Bearings reported a 66 percent rise in net profit to 188 million rupees after trading ended at the BSE.
SKF's shares stood unchanged at 2,450 rupees.
The Delhi index added 6.93 points to 707.98. The Calcutta index lost 2.26 points to 418.53 and the Madras index dropped 17.11 points to 3,1878.41.
-- ANSHUMAN DAGA, Bombay newsroom +91-22 265 9000
